finding: A 25th instance of the same bug class survives: AgentStepForm.tsx sits beside agentStepForm.ts. `.ts` is probed before `.tsx`, so `./AgentStepForm` (StepConfigPanel.tsx:5, workflow/gallery.tsx:556) resolves to the HELPER module on a case-insensitive filesystem. The branch's stated outcome (a green macOS build) is therefore not achieved.
fixed_in: agentStepForm.ts -> agentStepForm.helpers.ts (+ its test); 2 import sites updated
resolution: Independently re-verified: the pair exists, has exactly 2 non-self import sites, and a widened file-vs-file scan of src-app + sdk + scripts + agent-kit finds this and only this pair repo-wide.

finding: The guard's rule set (file-vs-dir + identical-full-name) is structurally blind to a file-vs-file stem collision across different extensions, so it reported the tree clean while AgentStepForm.tsx/agentStepForm.ts was live in it. Reproduced: a fixture of Foo.ts + foo.tsx exits 0.
fixed_in: new rule 2 (file-vs-file resolver-stem collision); TEST-2(b) pins it

finding: The guard misses `<Base>.desktop.<ext>` vs a sibling directory, which the desktop tier-2 resolver really creates (`probeDesktopInfix` probes `X.desktop.tsx` ahead of `X/`). This exact pair — ProviderGroupAssignmentCard.desktop.tsx vs providerGroupAssignmentCard/ — existed on origin/main; the store move dissolved it incidentally and nothing stopped it returning.
fixed_in: RESOLVER_INFIXES + resolverStems() emit the infix-stripped stem; TEST-2(c) pins it

finding: The guard FAILS OPEN: readdirSync errors were swallowed by `catch { return }`, and the scanned-directory count was a single aggregate, so pointing it at a non-existent root (`--root=src --root=../desktop/ui/srcXX`) still printed OK and exit 0. An unreadable directory (chmod 000) containing a real collision was likewise reported clean.
fixed_in: fail() on a missing/non-dir/unreadable root or dir; per-root counts reported; TEST-2(f) pins both

finding: TEST-6/TEST-7 assert `git diff origin/main...HEAD` is non-empty. Once merged, HEAD == origin/main, the diff is empty, and `npm run check` fails on main permanently — rule B6's failure mode reached through a branch-relative git assumption instead of a .lifecycle path. Reproduced on a simulated merged tree: 5 pass / 2 fail.
fixed_in: branchRenames() returns {available:false} with no base ref; both tests fall back to a durable tree-shape assertion. Re-verified by pointing refs/remotes/origin/main at HEAD: 7/7 pass, then restored.

finding: The anti-vacuity threshold `scannedFrom(out) > 300` is ~2x too loose and self-reported. Adding 'components' to the guard's SKIP_DIRS — skipping every subtree the 24 collisions lived in — drops 623 to 489 and the whole suite still passes; hardcoding the counter to a lie also passes.
fixed_in: the test now RECOMPUTES the directory count per contracted root and deepEqual's it against the guard's per-root report. Both mutations re-run here and both now turn TEST-1 RED.

finding: Clause 1 imported an explicit `/<path>/index.ts`, which skips extension probing entirely — the whole mechanism of the bug — so its failure message ('the case collision is back') was a phantom claim. Separately the `typeof mod[pascal] !== 'function'` discriminator was satisfied by an ABSENT value for 5 of 24 stores (measured in-browser), and the `.not.toContain('default')` leg's premise is false for 20 of 24 components.
fixed_in: clause 1 now imports the BARE directory specifier (verified served: curl of /modules/.../stores/editUserDrawer returns the store index), pairs each store with its component module, and asserts (a) the store exports something the component does not, (b) the component exports >=1 function (per-store control), (c) any shared name is not a function in the store. The 'default' leg is gone.

finding: TEST-8 asserted only `tsc --noEmit` exit 0, so a tsconfig that compiles NOTHING passes. Reproduced by replacing src-app/ui/tsconfig.json with {compilerOptions:{noEmit:true},files:[]} — the test stayed green. Its own control ran a different project in /tmp and therefore said nothing about the workspace invocation.
fixed_in: each workspace is now asserted three ways: exit 0, --listFilesOnly > 1000 files, and that list containing named relocated stores + their sibling components

finding: TEST-5's write leg is tautological (a passing --check already proves have === want, so an in-place rewrite cannot differ) AND it writes into the tracked source tree during `npm run check` — a gate with a side effect on the developer's working copy.
fixed_in: TEST-5 now copies both src trees to a temp dir, DELETES every actions.gen.ts, regenerates from scratch there, and asserts byte-identity with the committed files. Not implied by --check, and the tracked tree is never written.

finding: The spec header claims it proves appLayout's module-scope `appLayoutSeam.set(...)` side effect still fires. No assertion does; `appLayoutSeam` appears only in that comment. And the spec's own import of the module is what would set the seam, so an assertion in this shape would be self-fulfilling.
fixed_in: the claim is removed from the header rather than backed by a self-fulfilling assertion

finding: store-case-collision.spec.ts is in no visualSpecs list, no package.json chain, and no CI workflow — nothing runs it. TEST-3 explicitly asserts the UNIT suite is chained 'or the guard could rot untested'; the same reasoning was not applied to the spec.
fixed_in: added to gallery.config.json visualSpecs (so gate:ui runs it); TEST-3 now asserts that listing

finding: The tsc oracle file is referenced by no npm script and matched by no --test glob, so it never runs in any gate — dead code by CODING_GUIDELINES s15.
fixed_in: npm script test:case-collisions:tsc added; TEST-3 asserts it exists

finding: Guard roots omitted trees the same builds compile: src-app/ui/tests and src-app/desktop/ui/tests (both in tsconfig include) and sdk/packages/*/src (compiled through the @ziee/* path mappings). A collision in any of them breaks the macOS build identically. Currently zero findings, so latent.
fixed_in: defaultRoots() now covers 11 roots (both srcs, both tests dirs, every sdk package src); TEST-1 asserts the exact contracted set

finding: Symlinked entries were invisible (isFile() is false for a symlink and recursion required isDirectory()); duplicate/overlapping --root args double-counted a finding; rule 2 under-reported an N-way collision, naming only two of three names.
fixed_in: symlinks classified via statSync with an lstat fallback (named for collision purposes, not recursed into, keeping the walk acyclic); ROOTS deduped; findings deduped by (dir, name set) and rule 3 reports every distinct name

finding: The overlay assertion is identity-free: all 12 cases would pass identically if the gallery mounted the WRONG overlay, since nothing asserts which drawer opened. Also `&state=open` is inert (OverlayFrame fires open() unconditionally) yet reads as load-bearing, and the error-filter regex includes the bare word `undefined`, which risks false REDs on benign mock-API chatter.
fixed_in: each slug carries an expected-text regex asserted on the opened dialog; the inert param is dropped with a comment saying why; the regex is narrowed to the four shapes a bad specifier actually produces

finding: `preExisting` counted this branch's own 24 moves, so the 'the convention pre-dates us' assertion measured 115 against a >= 90 threshold — a margin of 1 over a number that included the thing under test.
fixed_in: preExisting now excludes the branch's relocated set (91 genuinely pre-existing, matching the design's own count)

finding: The file header's blanket 'every assertion here is BEHAVIOURAL / no source-text assertions' is untrue of TEST-3 (package.json strings) and TEST-4a (grep of the guard source).
fixed_in: header now names the two deliberate exceptions and why each cannot be behavioural

finding: No CI runs the new guard: the repo has only desktop-release.yml and server-release.yml, both tag-triggered, and neither runs `npm run check`. The macOS/Windows release build is the only automated backstop, and it has no PR trigger.
resolution: Out of scope by design s4 (in scope: the colliding pairs, their import sites, the regression guard). Adding a UI CI workflow to a repo that deliberately ships exactly two tag-triggered workflows (CLAUDE.md) is a separate change with its own review. Recorded in HUMAN_FEEDBACK.md and the PR body as a recommendation.

finding: The gallery entries for overlay-hub-model-details-drawer and overlay-hub-mcp-details-drawer render their component with no props, while both components begin `if (!model) return null` / `if (!server) return null`, so those overlays mount nothing regardless of the store. Pre-existing: neither component file is in this branch's diff.
resolution: Out of scope by design s4 (unrelated pre-existing debt). The two slugs are excluded from the spec's overlay list with the reasoning recorded inline (DRIFT-2.2); both stores remain covered by clause 1. Reported in HUMAN_FEEDBACK.md and the PR body.

finding: A prose comment still names the pre-move path modules/layouts/app-layout/appLayout.
fixed_in: comment updated to the new path

finding: The `surface:` string names modules/user/components/user/userGroupsDrawer, a path that no longer exists (the canonical surface is .../UserGroupsDrawer). Pre-existing lowercase typo, not introduced by the move.
resolution: I started to fix this and stopped after checking what it touches. Every generated registry already carries the PascalCase surface (coverage.ts, overlay-registry.generated.json, stateMatrix.generated.ts, STATE_MATRIX.md, galleryCoverage.generated.ts, stateCoverage.ts), and overlay-allowlist.json:12 allow-lists that PascalCase surface as 'not a standalone story'. Correcting the typo would make that surface wired-open, turn its allow-list entry stale, and fail `check:overlay-registry` until the entry is removed and several generated artifacts are regenerated — a generated-artifact cascade over pre-existing debt that design s4 puts out of scope. All four gallery gates pass as-is (verified). Reported in HUMAN_FEEDBACK.md and the PR body instead.

finding: TEST-3 is a wiring proof only: gutting the guard to `process.exit(0)` leaves it green.
resolution: Working as intended and stated at its site. TEST-2 covers the logic (13 independent mutations of the guard's behaviour were all killed by it); TEST-3's job is registration+chaining, which TEST-2 cannot see. The pair is complete; merging them would make one test answer two questions.

finding: No test in this branch runs on a case-INSENSITIVE filesystem, so the bug cannot reproduce in any of them; TEST-2(e) explicitly self-neuters on such a host.
resolution: Irreducible on this box (Linux, no Darwin toolchain) and acknowledged rather than papered over: the spec header now states plainly that clause 1 is a module-identity assertion and NOT a case-sensitivity simulation, and that the only true oracle is a macOS build. That build is recorded NOT VERIFIED in TEST_RESULTS.md for the lead to dispatch (DEC-12).

finding: Round 1's B6 fix only closed the post-merge case. TEST-6/TEST-7 are chained into `check`, so ANY future branch that relocates a store takes the branch path and fails `assert.equal(dirs.size, 24)`, and any branch cut from a stale base re-sees these 24 renames plus its own additions and fails the 'only renames' assertion. Reproduced with a git shim on PATH.
fixed_in: split into lint-case-collisions.provenance.test.mjs with its own runner, NOT chained into check (DEC-16). The chained suite is now entirely git-independent — grepping it for origin/main returns only comments. TEST-3 asserts the provenance suite is runnable by name AND absent from both check chains.

finding: The overlay identity regexes do not discriminate: /group/i matches three drawers and /provider/i two. Adversarially reproduced — navigate to slug A, assert slug B's regex: 8 of 10 cross-pairings PASSED. The spec's own docstring claims 'without the identity check, all 12 cases would pass identically if the gallery mounted the wrong overlay'; with the check, 8 of them still would.
fixed_in: replaced with per-drawer data-testid markers (captured from the live gallery), plus TEST-13 asserting the markers are mutually exclusive. Re-verified with the same adversarial cross-pairing: 0 of 132 wrong pairings pass, 12 of 12 correct ones do.

finding: test:case-collisions:tsc is in NO check chain, so its unique value — the --listFilesOnly non-empty-program assertion and the moved-files-in-program assertion — never executes. Reproduced: replacing src-app/ui/tsconfig.json with {compilerOptions:{noEmit:true},files:[]} left an exit-code-only version green. TEST-3 only asserted the script string exists, which is wiring, not logic.
fixed_in: chained into src-app/ui's check; DEC-13 CORRECTION records the reversal and why the original reasoning was wrong

finding: The guard scans the read-only sdk submodule with no allowlist and no opt-out, so an upstream collision would hard-block `npm run check` in both workspaces with no fixable path from this repo and no documented exit.
fixed_in: sdk roots are now ADVISORY: findings print in full and name the upstream repo but do not set a non-zero exit; the eight owned trees stay fail-closed. DEC-15. TEST-1 asserts the owned trees are NOT advisory, so the classification cannot be silently inverted.

finding: With sdk/ uninitialised the guard silently drops 7 of its 11 roots and prints a green OK — while the adjacent case (sdk/packages present but empty) is FATAL. The header claims 'a root that does not exist ... is a hard error, never a quiet OK'.
fixed_in: an explicit NOTE line names the missing submodule and says the @ziee/* sources were NOT scanned

finding: Extension and infix matching were case-SENSITIVE while the filesystem being modelled is not — two reproduced false negatives in a guard whose entire subject is case: `Foo.Desktop.tsx` beside `foo/` (probeDesktopInfix builds the literal foo.desktop.tsx, which stats as this on macOS) and `Widget.TSX` beside `widget/`, both exit 0.
fixed_in: both comparisons lowercased; TEST-2(g) pins three cases (.Desktop.tsx, .TSX, .MTS) and all three now exit 1

finding: A collision inside a symlinked directory is invisible AND the run still reports OK, naming nothing — the guard reports 'clean' for a tree it did not look at.
fixed_in: every symlinked directory that is named-but-not-walked now emits a NOTE saying so and how to scan it; TEST-2(i) pins it. Not walking them keeps the walk acyclic, which stays the right call.

finding: stemOwners was last-writer-wins, so when several files answer to one stem only one was named: `Foo.tsx` + `Foo.desktop.tsx` + `foo/` reported a single offender. The operator fixes half a pair and re-runs into the other half. This exact shape (component + .desktop override + store dir) was live on origin/main.
fixed_in: the map's value is a Set of filenames; TEST-2(h) asserts BOTH files are named

finding: Magic thresholds >= 110 and >= 90 sit ~5 and ~1 above the measured 115 / 91, so consolidating six store directories in a later refactor turns `npm run check` red with a message about case collisions that has nothing to do with the change.
fixed_in: replaced by TEST-12, which asserts the RATIO the claim actually makes (stores under a `stores/` ancestor > 2x those outside) instead of a count

finding: The guard's docstring claims it covers 'every tree the two UI builds actually COMPILE' but omitted both plugins/ dirs (desktop's IS compiled, via tsconfig.node.json -> vite.config.ts -> plugins/vite-plugin-local-override.ts) and both scripts/ dirs. Zero findings there today, so a coverage gap rather than a live bug.
fixed_in: both plugins/ and both scripts/ dirs added as mandatory roots (15 roots, 732 dirs); TEST-1's independent recount covers them

finding: Duplicate or nested --root arguments double-count the reported directory totals (dedup was on the resolved string only).
fixed_in: roots deduped by realpath, and a root nested inside another is dropped

finding: `galleryCfg.visualConfig?.visualSpecs ?? galleryCfg.visualSpecs` — the first branch is dead, since visualConfig is a STRING (the playwright config path).
fixed_in: dead branch removed; the test now asserts visualConfig is a string, so the shape is pinned rather than defensively guessed

finding: The `root scanned 0 directories` fail path is unreachable: scan() increments before anything can return, and any read error process.exit()s first.
fixed_in: still unreachable for mandatory roots by construction (which is the correct invariant), but now guarded on `!root.advisory` so the advisory path cannot fall into it. Kept as a cheap backstop rather than deleted.

finding: The .desktop infix rule is applied in desktop/ui/src, both tests/ dirs and sdk/packages/*/src, where no resolver probes that infix — over-strict.
resolution: Deliberate and documented at the site. The infix rule only ever ADDS a stem, so being over-strict can produce a false POSITIVE but never a false negative, and it has zero occupants outside the two app trees. Scoping it per-root would add a root-classification branch to buy nothing — the opposite of the bounded-rule-set property that keeps this guard out of GUARD-SUB territory.

finding: TEST-1's 'independent recount' did not close the vacuity hole it claimed to. It measured directories TRAVERSED, not entries ANALYSED, so a mutation that recurses into `components/` but performs no collision analysis there kept every count byte-identical: a planted collision at src/modules/user/components/ went undetected with the full suite at 6 pass / 0 fail. That is exactly where the 24 real collisions lived.
fixed_in: the guard now reports ENTRIES ANALYSED, counted at the point of analysis, and countEntries() recomputes that independently. I re-applied the mutation after the fix and TEST-1 turns RED.

finding: No test proved that a finding in a mandatory DEFAULT root causes exit 1. Every RED fixture passes --root=, which is a different code path (hardcoded mandatory) aimed at a flat temp dir; the default-root classification was only ever exercised on a clean tree. Reproduced: adding a `blocks:false` flag to the defaults (leaving the `advisory` label TEST-1 checks untouched) let a planted collision in src-app/ui/src print OK and exit 0, suite green.
fixed_in: TEST-15 builds a synthetic repo with the real script at the real relative path and runs it with NO ARGS: clean, blocking-in-components, advisory-only, and both-at-once. Re-applying the decoupling mutation now turns TEST-15 RED.

finding: An advisory-only run printed the full sdk collision report and then `OK - no sibling names differ only by case`. The green line is what a reader — and TEST-1's own assert.match — skims for.
fixed_in: a distinct line: 'no BLOCKING collisions in the trees this repo owns, but N advisory finding(s) remain upstream'. TEST-15(c) asserts the unqualified green line does NOT follow an advisory report.

finding: MUST_COMPILE hardcodes branch-specific paths (.../stores/editUserDrawer/index.ts, agentStepForm.helpers.ts) in a file that this same round chained into `npm run check`. A future branch that legitimately renames or consolidates editUserDrawer gets a red build with a case-collision message about a change it knows nothing about — the same one-time-claim-in-a-permanent-gate defect the provenance split was performed to remove. The file's header also still claimed it was NOT chained.
fixed_in: mustCompile() derives a store/component pair from the tree at runtime; the header now states the chaining and why

finding: The 'does not apply here' fallback was a disguised skip: its residual assertion was fs.existsSync(<UI>/src), which cannot be false in any tree where the test file exists. Reproduced in a non-git copy: both tests report ok, '# pass 2', having verified nothing — a green certificate for INV-4/INV-7 backed by no evidence, in a suite whose entire purpose is to certify them once.
fixed_in: requireEvaluable() now HARD-FAILS with an explanatory message when origin/main is unresolvable or the diff relocates no store. Verified by deleting refs/remotes/origin/main: 0 pass / 2 fail with the explanatory text, then restored.

finding: The 'markers are mutually exclusive' test inspects the OVERLAYS array and never touches the DOM, so the property it needs — marker M appears in drawer D and no other — is unproven. Two drawers rendering the same testid (the realistic regression, since two markers come from one shared component via a testidPrefix prop) would pass unchanged.
fixed_in: replaced by a DOM cross-check that opens all 12 drawers and tests all 144 marker/drawer combinations, asserting every off-diagonal cell fails. 14/14 pass.

finding: Three markers were coupled to seeded data or permissions: `user-groups-drawer-list` renders only on the groups.length > 0 branch, and the two `*-group-assign-save-btn` only inside {canManage && …}. A fixture or permission change would turn a case-collision spec red with a message about the wrong drawer.
fixed_in: those three now use drawer TITLE text, which depends on neither seeded data nor seeded permissions

finding: TEST-3's separation claim was a literal-string doesNotMatch, bypassed two ways that both put the provenance suite back inside `check`: an indirection script, or invoking the file directly with node --test.
fixed_in: the chain is now expanded TRANSITIVELY through npm run references and the assertion runs over the expansion, matching both the script name and the file path

finding: TEST-12's ratio is satisfiable with the convention fully violated: moving all 24 relocated stores back OUT of stores/ leaves 95-vs-36, which still clears `> 2x`. Its per-store loop was also a tautology (asserting index.ts exists on a list built by that predicate), and requiring `actions/` dropped 45 outside-convention store dirs from the denominator.
fixed_in: the population statistic is GONE — it cannot express a per-store claim. TEST-12 now asserts only what a whole-tree check honestly can: every dir under a stores/ ancestor defines a store or is a barrel, and none collides with a sibling. The per-store placement claim lives in TEST-7 (provenance), where it belongs. The new predicate immediately caught a real false positive of its own (llmModelDrawers/index.ts is a barrel), which is fixed.

finding: The nesting-drop ran across the whole root list ignoring classification and compared REALPATHS, so a mandatory root whose realpath landed inside an advisory root was dropped, its tree walked only under the advisory root, and all its findings became advisory — fail-OPEN, with the root silently absent from the scope line. Reproduced with src-app/ui/plugins symlinked into sdk. Separately, a root under another root's SKIP_DIRS was dropped and then scanned by nobody.
fixed_in: SIMPLIFIED rather than hardened: --root= now takes exactly one directory, which deletes the dedup/nesting machinery and both defects with it. Neither shape had a real caller — the defaults are disjoint by construction and every test passes one root.

finding: The `root scanned 0 directories` fail-closed check is unreachable dead code: scan() increments before anything can return and its only readdir failure path is fail(). A fail-closed guard that can never fire reads as safety it does not provide.
fixed_in: deleted, with a comment naming the real protections (the root statSync and TEST-1's independent recount)

finding: All three rules compare siblings inside ONE directory, but the desktop resolver's Tier 1 resolves a core-tree specifier against the DESKTOP tree — so desktop/ui/src/x/Foo.tsx beside ui/src/x/foo/ diverges identically and no rule sees it. Pre-existing, and zero such pairs today, but this diff's header asserts the rule set is BOUNDED because 'each rule maps to a real resolver probe', and Tier 1 is a real probe with no rule.
fixed_in: NOT by adding a fourth rule — that is the predicate-piling GUARD-SUB warns against. The header now states the limit explicitly, and TEST-14 (the resolution oracle) is the backstop: it diffs OUTCOMES over real specifiers, so it is not blind to shapes the sibling rules cannot express.

finding: TEST-6 and TEST-7 disagreed on the same degraded input: with a low diff.renameLimit, git emits A/D for a rename WITH content changes, so TEST-7 degraded gracefully while TEST-6 hard-failed on `src-app/ui/src must contain only renames`.
fixed_in: the A/D assertion is scoped to files inside the relocated store directories, which is the claim INV-4 actually makes; an unrelated helper test renamed with edits no longer breaks it. Verified under diff.renameLimit=1: 2/2 pass.

finding: The symlink fixture tested only the NOTICE, not the other half of the claim: deleting `dirs.push(e.name)` from the symlink branch (so a symlinked dir can no longer collide with a sibling stem) passed 6/6.
fixed_in: a second fixture asserts a symlinked directory still COLLIDES with a sibling file stem (exit 1)

finding: expectedRoots() calls readdirSync(sdkPackages) unguarded, so without the submodule TEST-1 dies with an opaque ENOENT rather than an assertion — the test is less robust than the thing it tests. Also `new RegExp(file.replace('.', '\.'))` escapes only the FIRST dot.
fixed_in: an explicit assertion naming `git submodule update --init`; replaceAll for the escape

finding: toLowerCase() does not fold Turkish dotted/dotless I or eszett, so those fixtures exit 0.
resolution: Not a defect, and the auditor said so too: APFS and NTFS do not equate those either, so matching their folding is correct behaviour rather than a gap. Every filename in both trees is ASCII.

finding: Proportionality: the checking apparatus is 1,915 lines against a +135/-115 fix (14:1) and adds +49s to every `npm run check`, 47s of it a duplicate two-workspace tsc pass -- making this branch the most expensive item in the gate at ~2.4x the cost of the type-check it protects. The round-3 commit message diagnosed guard-substitution and then added a fifth script while keeping four.
fixed_in: tsc oracle un-chained (-47s), resolution oracle chained in its place (+0.3s), numeric floors deleted. Gate goes from +49s to ~+2s and gets more general.

finding: `src-app/ui`'s check now type-checks the DESKTOP workspace and reports failures as case-collision failures: a type error in desktop/ui makes ui's gate red with 'at least one import site still points at a pre-move path'. It also asserted the desktop program contains ui/src store paths.
fixed_in: un-chained from `check` (keeps its runner, runs at phase 8); TEST-3 now asserts it is NOT chained, with the coupling reason at the site

finding: The resolution oracle resolved `@/` only against ui/src -- tier 3 only -- so it was exactly as blind to the desktop resolver's cross-tree Tier 1 as the sibling rules the guard's header says it backstops. Reproduced with a faithful port of resolveOverridePath: real resolver diverges (linux=ui/src/x/foo/index.ts, macos=desktop/ui/src/x/Foo.tsx), the test reports no divergence.
fixed_in: specifierBases() returns all three desktop tiers in probe order and resolveTiered() takes the first hit; a tier-1 control asserts the divergence IS detected. 0 such pairs today, confirmed over all 623 @/ specifiers.

finding: 'Every real import specifier' omitted ~12%: ~570 @ziee/* subpath aliases (incl. @ziee/desktop/modules/updater/stores/updater -- the exact shape this branch is about, and the only route by which the oracle could cover the advisory sdk trees), ~90 side-effect imports (`import './types'`) unmatched by the regex, TS's .js->.ts substitution unmodelled, and desktop's exact @/api-client/* mappings resolved into the wrong tree.
fixed_in: PKG_ALIASES + DESKTOP_EXACT + a side-effect-import alternative in SPEC_RE + JS_TO_TS substitution

finding: The entries-analysed counter sat BEFORE the rule blocks, so any early return between counter and rules leaves the number byte-identical -- the exact mutation its 10-line comment claims to catch. Reproduced over a full copy of the real trees: identical counts (4284/2830), planted collision undetected, TEST-1 still green. The protection came from TEST-15, not from where the comment attributed it.
fixed_in: counted after all three rules have run over the directory's entries; comment corrected to say why placement matters

finding: The guard and its independent recount disagree on symlinks: Dirent.isDirectory()/isFile() are both false for a symlink so countEntries skipped them, while the guard statSyncs and counts them. The pre-round-3 pair agreed; round 3 broke it. Latent (zero symlinks today) but would turn `npm run check` red for an unrelated change the day one appeared -- and this branch is actively extending the guard's symlink handling.
fixed_in: countEntries classifies symlinks by target exactly as the guard does, and does not recurse into symlinked dirs. Verified equal on a fixture (2 = 2).

finding: Round 3's hard-fail made the provenance suite permanently RED on main: a named, documented, runnable npm script that can never pass again after merge, which TEST-3 simultaneously forbids removing. Reproduced in a throwaway repo with origin/main == HEAD: 0 pass / 2 fail.
fixed_in: rewritten on `git log --follow` -- a rename is recorded in history permanently, so the claim is true on the branch AND on main. Verified with refs/remotes/origin/main deleted entirely: 2/2 pass.

finding: The anti-vacuity floors cannot detect the loss of an entire workspace: measured UI-only = 6733 examined vs DESKTOP-only = 223, so every global floor passes on the web workspace alone while the headline claim ('either UI workspace') is half unverified.
fixed_in: per-workspace tallies with their own floors

finding: `.css` in PROBE_EXTS is a false-positive vector: no resolver extension-probes .css for a relative specifier, so `./styles` beside styles/index.ts and Styles.css was flagged as a macOS break that cannot occur. Separately readDir's bare catch failed OPEN on EACCES, returning an empty listing identically under both regimes so an unreadable subtree contributes zero divergences.
fixed_in: .css removed with the reason at the site; readDir now rethrows anything that is not ENOENT/ENOTDIR

finding: The oracle claims to catch divergence 'whatever shape produced it', but a full-name case duplicate (Foo.ts beside foo.ts) is invisible: statAs checks the exact name before folding, so both regimes return it. Rule 3 of the shape guard does catch it, so no live hole -- the claim is what is wrong.
fixed_in: header now states the shape it cannot see and names rule 3 as the complement, rather than claiming shape-independence

finding: mustCompile()'s early-out is checked per walk frame rather than per iteration (returns 4 paths, not 3), and its needles became ABSOLUTE while `tsc --listFilesOnly` prints realpaths -- so a worktree reached through a symlinked path goes red with 'the moved module is outside the compile surface'.
fixed_in: needles are repo-relative again; the early-out is checked inside the loop

finding: The DOM cross-check probes with non-retrying isVisible()/textContent(), so a marker rendering one tick after the dialog becomes visible fails the diagonal with a message blaming the marker.
fixed_in: the diagonal retries for 5s; the off-diagonal deliberately does not (waiting for a marker that should never appear would cost 132 timeouts)

finding: Three doc claims contradict the code shipped alongside them: the guard's usage line still said `--root` is repeatable 90 lines above the block comment explaining it is not; the provenance header still described the graceful fallback requireEvaluable replaced; the resolution header's '~10-20s' (the sole stated reason for not chaining it) measured 0.26s.
fixed_in: all three corrected; the provenance file was rewritten wholesale

finding: Numeric floors reintroduced in the chained suite directly below an exact-equality recount that subsumes them (`> 2000` vs actual 2830; `stores.length > 100` vs 120) -- the drifting-threshold class TEST-12's own comment complains about.
fixed_in: all redundant floors deleted; TEST-12 carries no count at all now, only a per-store assertion

finding: The control test wrote its temp dir into the REPO ROOT (`.resolution-control-*`, not gitignored) while every sibling fixture uses os.tmpdir(); a crash before the finally leaves an untracked directory that could trip a cleanliness gate.
fixed_in: os.tmpdir(), with the reason at the site

finding: `git log --follow` cannot distinguish `git mv` from a same-commit cp+rm — git stores snapshots and detects renames by content similarity at query time, so both produce byte-identical history. Reproduced by relocating a 22-store tree with cp -r + rm -rf, never invoking git mv: the real unmodified test passed 2/2, and --follow still reported R100. The header claimed the opposite and the failure string 'it was copied, not moved' was unreachable by construction.
fixed_in: header now states plainly that INV-4's MECHANISM is not machine-checkable, and that what is asserted is the design's purpose clause ('so history follows the files'), which is checkable and is what the test proves

finding: TEST-6 asserted every candidate crosses a relocation rename, so a legitimately NEW store created in place under stores/ fails it with 'it was copied, not moved'. Reproduced: 22 properly-moved stores plus one new one -> 1 pass / 1 fail. Third instance on this branch of a permanent check carrying a claim that only holds for this tree.
fixed_in: shape is asserted only on the renames that EXIST; the population assertion is 'at least one store shows the relocation', which is durable

finding: A shallow clone is mis-diagnosed: `git log --follow` on a --depth 1 checkout exits 0 with EMPTY output, so the `status !== 0` branch never fires and the carefully-written 'cannot read history / run in a full clone' message is unreachable. The test instead blames a copy that never happened.
fixed_in: history() now returns commit depth alongside renames, and 'no history' is distinguished from 'no rename' with the right message for each

finding: The 8-of-24 sample is readdir-ORDER dependent (adding an unrelated directory reshuffles which 8 are checked) and its stated justification is false: 24 --follow calls cost 4.0s vs 1.3s for 8, in a manual phase-8-only suite.
fixed_in: checks all candidates; the `>= 20` floor is gone with it

finding: Every coverage widening added in round 4 could be reverted with the suite staying GREEN — the desktop tiers, the @ziee/* aliases, the side-effect-import pattern, and JS_TO_TS were each reverted in turn and the main test passed each time, because the anti-vacuity floors have enough headroom (34-67%) to absorb thousands of dropped specifiers. The diff's headline improvements were entirely unprotected.
fixed_in: a coverage control asserts specifierBases() output shape directly (web=1 base, desktop=3 tiers in order, DESKTOP_EXACT, @ziee/* roots, bare package skipped) and SPEC_RE's side-effect matching; a .js->.ts fixture pins JS_TO_TS. All three previously-surviving mutations re-run here and all three now go RED.

finding: JS_TO_TS was applied AFTER the literal probe; tsc strips the .js extension BEFORE probing (confirmed with --traceResolution: "has a '.js' extension - stripping it"). So `./foo.js` with Foo.js + foo.ts present reported a divergence (foo.ts vs Foo.js) that real tsc cannot produce — it never stats foo.js. Latent: only 2 .js files exist under either src.
fixed_in: substitution moved ahead of the literal probe, with tsc's traced order quoted at the site

finding: Deleting the tree-size floors was justified as 'subsumed by the exact recount'. It is not, and that was falsified by construction: the recount proves the guard AGREES WITH an independent walk, which stays true on a degenerate tree where both walk almost nothing. A layout with the right root structure but 3 entries under src-app/ui/src passed TEST-1; with the floors pasted back it failed.
fixed_in: floors restored with the falsification recorded at the site — they measure a different property (the tree is REAL) from the recount (the guard AGREES)

finding: TEST-12 after round 4 passed on a tree containing exactly ONE store (23 of 24 deleted), and never opened index.ts at all — so every stores/*/index.ts could be empty and it stayed green. Removing the defeatable RATIO was right; removing the reality anchor with it was not.
fixed_in: population anchor and the defines-a-store check restored; the ratio stays gone

finding: Un-chaining the tsc oracle is coverage-safe for INV-3 (both workspaces' own `check` starts with tsc) but it did lose the non-empty-program legs: nothing in either chain now notices a tsconfig narrowed to compile almost nothing. Also, the resolution oracle skips specifiers that resolve nowhere under both regimes, so a planted missed import with no case twin is invisible to it.
fixed_in: TEST-16 restores exactly that leg, ui-only (no cross-workspace coupling) and via --listFilesOnly (~2s, no type-check)

finding: The tsc exclusion was a naive doesNotMatch on the check string — bypassed by one indirection — while the provenance exclusion five lines below got a transitive-reachability walk. Same bypass class, two standards, failing open.
fixed_in: both exclusions now run over the transitively-expanded chain

finding: The header justified chaining with 'reachable by no runner at all (dead code, CODING_GUIDELINES s15)'. False: `test:case-collisions:resolution` already existed in package.json before the change. The same diff simultaneously argued in the sibling tsc file that un-chained-but-has-a-runner is fine — one diff, two readings of s15.
fixed_in: the s15 overreach is withdrawn in the header; the real argument (the general oracle belongs in the gate) is stated instead

finding: The header cited `{"compilerOptions":{"noEmit":true},"files":[]}` as a VERIFIED demonstration that an empty program exits 0. It does not reproduce — tsc rejects an empty files list with TS18002, exit 2. A header citing a check that does not reproduce is the false-assurance shape the file exists to remove.
fixed_in: corrected in place (a narrowed `include` is the shape that really slips through), with the correction left visible rather than the sentence deleted

finding: `assert.match(check, /npm run test:case-collisions\b/)` is satisfied by `test:case-collisions:resolution` alone, because the word boundary matches before the colon — so dropping the base suite from the chain would go unnoticed.
fixed_in: anchored with a (?=\s|$) lookahead instead of \b

finding: The diagonal retry is a busy-wait: `do { … } while (Date.now() < deadline)` with no delay fires thousands of CDP round-trips per second of retry.
fixed_in: 100ms poll interval; the off-diagonal still does not retry, so the adversarial half is unchanged

finding: Only the FINAL path segment is case-folded, so a mis-cased intermediate directory (`./Stores/foo` against a real `stores/foo`) is invisible. Also: the three desktop tiers are applied only to specifiers in desktop-tree FILES, while the plugin is not importer-scoped, and tier 2 is modelled through the full probe chain where the real probeDesktopInfix only tries `<rel>.desktop.<ext>`.
resolution: Documented as KNOWN LIMITS in the header rather than modelled, deliberately. Each was measured at zero live occurrences (0 divergences with core-file tiering applied; no `*.desktop` paths in either tree; tsc catches the mis-cased segment because it is unresolvable on Linux, and tsc is check's first step). Expanding the model to cover three latent shapes would re-inflate the artifact this round is shrinking — the honest move is to state what it does not cover so no other file's header leans on it.
